mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court of Korea having jurisdiction over the company's registered principal office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication path A for Apostille Convention countries: Korean notary public notarization and then Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille certificate. Authentication path B for non-Apostille countries: Korean notary public notarization and then consular legalization by the diplomatic or consular representative of the destination country in Korea. Paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Corporate Registration Particulars and Certificate of No Tax Delinquency)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court registry and National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille states: notarize the underlying court and tax certificates and obtain a single Apostille from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-Apostille states: notarize and submit directly to the destination country's consular official for consular legalization; no Apostille is used and the two methods are never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney for Incorporation and Bank Opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issued by the Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa and attested by the corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy of the resolution is notarized in Korea. If the receiving jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention member, the document receives an MOFA Apostille. If it is a non-member, the document receives consular legalization from the receiving state's consulate in Korea. The two paths are parallel and exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter of the Chusik Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The notarized Articles are authenticated by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille for Apostille member jurisdictions. For non-member jurisdictions, the notarized Articles are legalized by the receiving jurisdiction's embassy or consulate in Korea in the parallel path; no combined apostille-consular chain is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank where the company maintains its first corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank issues the reference letter on bank letterhead; if the addressee requires authentication, the bank officer's signature is notarized and, only where required, an Apostille is obtained from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the destination is an Apostille state. For non-Apostille destinations, consular legalization of the notarized signature is used exclusively; no Apostille is obtained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration and Certificate of Corporate Seal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Representative director of the Chusik Hoesa and the court registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The UBO declaration is notarized and then subject to either Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on the destination state's Convention membership; the certificate of corporate seal is issued by the court registry and follows the same parallel, exclusive authentication path.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, ultimate controllers, and counterparties must be screened before and continuously after incorporation against the OFAC SDN list, OFAC non-SDN lists, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU consolidated sanctions list, the Republic of Korea's FATF-aligned lists maintained by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and law-enforcement watchlists. For each customer the entity will apply risk-based CDD-EDD including PEP status, foreign PEPs, family members and close associates, state-owned enterprise control, adverse media, persons holding more than 25% ownership or exercising de facto control, and source-of-wealth verification. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years under Article 5A of the Korean AML Act and FATF Recommendation 12.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (Internet Registration; court registry name-search and corporate registration system)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registration is maintained in Hangul. The statutory corporate form must appear as Chusik Hoesa or its Hangul equivalent; a foreign-language name may be recorded as a secondary trade name if transliterated into Hangul. Four-tier naming convention: (1) distinctive brand or identifier; (2) business object description; (3) corporate form suffix Chusik Hoesa; and (4) geographical or unique qualifier. The name cannot be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name in the same or similar business under the Commercial Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed name, the attorney should first request in writing the detailed grounds from the registration official within seven days. If rejection is confirmed, an administrative appeal may be filed with the competent district court under the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days, but practical practice is to promptly reserve a revised name with a distinctive qualifier and no prohibited token. The registry does not grant extension of the 30-day reservation; a fresh search and reservation is required. Pre-filing advisory review and simultaneous reservation of backup names reduce delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a social casino and virtual slots software publisher, a non-physical virtual office or commercial mailbox is not advisable and will likely be rejected by the National Tax Service for business registration and by regulated banks for corporate account onboarding. Korean commercial registry law requires the principal office to be stated with a precise address and to constitute the actual place of management; tax officials may treat a mail-only address as an unregistered business place. A business lounge with a dedicated desk, lease, local personnel, and the ability to receive tax notices can be accepted, but only for a limited period; for this gaming-adjacent sector, physical substance is expected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-High, approximately 40-50% during the first 12 months for gambling-adjacent software companies. Tax offices may perform unannounced field inspections under VAT and corporate tax rules; registry officials can verify the principal office; banks conduct EDD site visits. Checklist: maintain the current lease and utility bills in the company's name; office nameplate and mail delivery; at least one local employee; payroll and accounting ledgers; board minutes and statutory registers physically available; corporate seal and seal certificate; AML-CFT manual; evidence that the registered office is the true place of management.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 9975, as amended), Articles 288 through 317 (Formation and Registration of Stock Corporations); Article 295 (Payment of Subscription Price); Article 317 (Application for Incorporation Registration); Article 329(4) (Minimum Par Value of Shares)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court in whose jurisdiction the Company's registered office is located, administered through the Supreme Court of Korea Registration System (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation under Article 317 of the Korean Commercial Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Korean Commercial Act imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. The subscribers must, however, pay in full the aggregate par value of the subscribed shares before the incorporation registration is completed. Each issued share must have a par value of at least KRW 100. The paid-in capital is not subject to an escrow or blocked-account regime; provided, however, the funds must be deposited into a designated capital payment bank account in the Republic of Korea and must remain in that account until the legal existence of the Company is registered and the restriction on withdrawals under Articles 295 and 302 of the Commercial Act is lifted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CHUSIK HOESA (THE COMPANY), A LIMITED LIABILITY STOCK CORPORATION ORGANIZED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA.

The Board of Directors of the Company, duly convened on the ____ day of __________, 20____, at the registered office of the Company, with all directors present in person, or validly participating through written waiver or proxy, after due deliberation, unanimously adopted the following resolutions:

1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT. RESOLVED, that the Company shall duly and irrevocably issue, and each promoter and subscriber named in the incorporating instruments shall subscribe for, the aggregate number of ordinary shares specified in the minutes of the incorporators' meeting, each share having a par value of KRW 100 or such other lawful par value as stated in the Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the full subscription price for each issued share shall be paid in lawful currency of the Republic of Korea into the capital payment account maintained at a bank duly authorized to receive incorporation deposits, prior to the submission of the Application for Registration of Incorporation. The bank's certificate of deposit shall be delivered to the registered office of the Company and preserved in the statutory corporate records.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be the physical address set forth in the notarized Articles of Incorporation, which address lies within the territorial jurisdiction of the Republic of Korea. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Board shall execute or cause to be executed a legally binding lease agreement or any form of legally valid premises arrangement for such registered office, pay all charges required for its occupation, and present documentary proof of address to the competent Court Registry at the time of incorporation registration.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION AND EXECUTIVE SIGNATURES. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open, or cause to be opened, one or more corporate operating accounts at a commercial bank licensed by the Financial Services Commission of the Republic of Korea. The Chief Executive Officer or representative director, the Chief Financial Officer, and any other duly authorized officer shall be designated accountable signatories. RESOLVED FURTHER, that every withdrawal, transfer, corporate guarantee, loan agreement, or payment commitment exceeding KRW 10,000,000 or its foreign-currency equivalent shall require the joint signature of two duly authorized signatories, unless otherwise approved by a unanimous board resolution.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers are hereby elected and appointed: (a) a representative director, who shall have the authority to conduct the ordinary business of the Company, to execute contracts, and to represent the Company before registry authorities, tax authorities, and commercial counterparties; (b) a statutory auditor, or an audit committee if applicable, selected in compliance with Articles 408 through 415 of the Korean Commercial Act; and (c) a company secretary responsible for maintenance of shareholder register, board minutes, statutory filings, and corporate records. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all such officers shall accept their offices in writing and shall faithfully perform their duties under the Commercial Act, the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, and Korean corporate governance standards.

5. DELEGATION AND POST-INCORPORATION ACTION. RESOLVED, that the representative director is authorized, either alone or jointly with counsel, to execute all incorporation registration applications, to obtain the business registration certificate from the National Tax Service, to file the corporate seal certificate application, to open payment and settlement accounts for the Company's digital content services, and to take all lawful steps necessary to commence software publishing operations in the Republic of Korea.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Service (iRO) and a duly commissioned Korean Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Counsel shall verify the proposed company name in Korean and English against the Supreme Court's Internet Registration Service name-search database to ensure no identical or confusingly similar name is reserved. After clearance, counsel shall prepare the Articles of Incorporation containing (i) the exact corporate name, (ii) the corporate object limited to software publishing, social casino simulation content and game distribution, (iii) total authorized shares, (iv) par value per share, (v) initial subscribed capital, (vi) registered office address, and (vii) statutory officer identities. All incorporators shall sign or execute by proxy, and the articles shall be notarized before a Korean notary public under the Commercial Act. The notarized text is then retained for filing.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of each incorporator
Notarized power of attorney for foreign incorporators, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search returns a conflicting identical or similar name, counsel shall promptly submit a second-choice name. If the notary raises any defect in the draft articles, the incorporators shall amend and re-execute the affected pages, and a new notarization shall be obtained within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment and Verification of Subscribed Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank authorized by the Financial Services Commission of the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: No statutory minimum capital applies; nevertheless, the amount represented at formation must be actually paid before registration. The promoter(s) must open, at a Korean bank, a designated capital payment account in the name of the company or its promoter, and deposit the aggregate subscription amount in KRW. The bank will issue a deposit certificate showing the balance, the account holder, and the date. This certificate is an essential attachment to the registration request. The funds must remain deposited and available until registration; they may be used only after the corporate legal personality becomes effective. If the company fails to register, the funds shall be returned to subscribers under applicable law.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation for bank due diligence
Anti-money laundering declaration and source-of-funds evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue a deposit certificate because the account title does not match the proposed corporate name or because the identity documents are incomplete, counsel shall correct the bank's account registration to the exact corporate name, supplement the anti-money laundering questionnaire, and request a revised certificate on the next business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Incorporation Registration with the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Commercial Registration Office in the jurisdiction of the registered office, via the Korean Supreme Court e-Registration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Counsel shall submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation to the District Court Commercial Registration Office in whose territory the registered office is located. Submitted documents must include notarized articles, capital deposit certificate, signed acceptances of office by directors and auditor, minutes of incorporators' meeting, identity certificate of each statutory officer, lease or certificate of address for the registered office, and duly notarized powers of attorney if any foreign director or shareholder signs through proxy. The registrar will examine the documents; upon approval, the court assigns a corporate registration number and the company legally exists. Any defect listed in the registrar's supplementary order must be cured before registration can occur.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation
Written consent/acceptance of office of each director and auditor
Certificate of registered office address (lease agreement or ownership certificate)
Notarized powers of attorney for foreign signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplemental order or refuses the filing, counsel shall prepare the exact corrected document and re-file within the prescribed supplemental period. If the refusal is substantive, counsel shall file an application for rectification or appeal to the competent court within the statutory appeal period. Any change requiring amendment of the Articles must first be approved by shareholders and re-notarized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and Corporate Seal Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax portal or the local District Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after the court registration, the representative director shall file the business opening registration with the National Tax Service through HomeTax or a local district tax office, using the company registration certificate and corporate seal. The NTS grants a business registration number and issues a corporate seal certificate. The company must also open a corporate operating bank account in the name of the legal entity, register for four major social insurances if hiring employees, and post statutory labor and safety notices. This step ensures the entity is able to issue tax invoices, pay corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding income tax, and contract lawfully with customers.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NTS rejects registration due to inconsistent registered office or missing seals, cure by submitting the lease contract and court registration certificate. If rejection arises from representative identity issues, submit a notarized foreign identification document and, if needed, designate a Korean resident agent for tax notices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Game Distribution Compliance and Financial Fraud Controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Game Rating and Administration Committee (GRAC) and Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KOFIU)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The game build and metadata must be submitted to the Korea Game Rating and Administration Committee before the game can be offered on domestic mobile stores. The submission package includes the completed rating request, working APK/IPA or searchable link, detailed game flow, art assets, store age-grade ranking, and the in-app purchase design. Counsel shall ensure that the virtual slots and casual social casino functions do not permit any mechanism converting virtual chips into cash or valuables, because such mechanism is prohibited under Korean speculative gaming law. A sign-off memorandum from counsel on this point is retained internally. The company shall also appoint a compliance officer to monitor IAP fraud and money laundering.
required_dossiers: Game build, APK/IPA, or private link
Game script and user flow diagrams
In-app purchase policy and payment flow documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GRAC remands the rating request due to prohibited gambling mechanics, the company must re-engineer the game to remove cash-out or virtual-to-real value conversion and resubmit. If KOFIU flags the transaction model, the company shall amend the in-app purchase terms, add explicit player prohibitions against conversion, and produce enhanced transaction monitoring reports.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. This entity is a pure digital software publisher under ISIC 5820; no industrial licensing board, municipal manufacturing authority, or physical industrial establishment is triggered. Digital game content is overseen by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the Korea Game Rating and Administration Committee, not by an industrial operating license regime.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — no operating license, manufacturing permit, warehouse permit, chemical permit, assembly license, or physical industrial license is required for the publishing of simulated social casino and virtual slots games.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea / Korea Environment Corporation (triggered only for physical projects; not applicable to this digital publisher)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Triggered. The company is a pure digital software publisher operating in a commercial office environment, with no construction, manufacturing, mining, energy generation, wastewater treatment, hazardous waste storage, or physical emission source listed in the Environmental Impact Assessment Act Enforcement Decree.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: 0 t/yr regulated wastewater discharge; 0 t/yr VOC emissions; 0 t/yr hazardous waste generation; 0 t/yr particulate emissions. Waste electrical and electronic equipment, if any, shall be routed exclusively to government-approved recyclers under the Act on Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources.

If the Company leases a physical office, the landlord's building use permit and fire-safety certificate must be on file at the premises. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the Company must maintain general workplace safety rules, provide employee safety training, and display a workplace safety policy. No civil defense fire permit is separately obtainable by the tenant for software-only office activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: National Tax Service HomeTax system (hometax.go.kr). For customs clearance, the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS single window is the operative platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Confirm that the foreign Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) has no domestic place of business in Korea but is engaged in taxable supplies of electronic services to Korean or foreign users. Step 2 - Appoint a statutory tax representative in Korea, as required by the Framework Act on National Taxes, and execute a power of attorney with prescribed due-diligence documentation. Step 3 - Prepare the corporate attestation package: certificate of foreign incorporation, articles of incorporation, board resolution authorizing the Korean tax representative, and the representative's identification and address evidence. Step 4 - Submit the official Business Registration Application to the National Tax Service through the HomeTax electronic platform, or to the competent district tax office; foreign non-resident taxpayers are ordinarily assigned to the Seoul Regional Tax Office. Step 5 - After NTS verification, obtain the Business Registration Certificate with the statutory 10-digit Business Registration Number, which simultaneously constitutes the VAT identification number and corporate reference number; this number is mandatory for issuing electronic tax invoices. Step 6 - Activate e-tax invoice issuance credentials and file, if required, the VAT mandatory registration particulars within the statutory time frame using the appointed tax representative for non-resident persons.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - The Chusik Hoesa is a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act, taxed on worldwide income as a separate entity under progressive corporate tax rates; no pass-through eligibility.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - Korean tax law contains no check-the-box election or treaty-based transparent entity election for a Chusik Hoesa. Hybrid mismatch effects are addressed through the Framework Act on International Tax Adjustment's structured arrangement adjustment provisions, but the entity itself cannot elect domestic classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act, administered nationwide by the National Tax Service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold: every business operator supplying taxable goods or services in Korea must register, including foreign electronic service suppliers, from the first taxable supply. Small traders may be eligible for simplified VAT taxation only after meeting qualitative criteria, but registration remains compulsory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) for all B2B taxable supplies, issued and transmitted to the NTS e-tax invoice system through the HomeTax portal, bureau-approved EDI/ERP API integrations, or certified digital platforms. The invoice must include the Business Registration Number, supply description, supply date and 10% VAT. Transmission must take place by the statutory deadline; no separate real-time fiscal clearance stamp is issued, but the NTS performs continuous cross-matching and anti-fraud verification. Late, missing or false e-invoices are subject to penalty surcharges under the VAT Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated upon evidenced customs export. Qualified services, including digital game content, in-app virtual currency and social casino software published under ISIC 5820, supplied to customers resident outside Korea and actually used or performed outside Korea may be zero-rated through the foreign exchange earning arrangement. For the present app-store distribution model, eligibility requires non-resident end-user location evidence and foreign currency receipts remitted into Korea, with the economic benefit enjoyed outside Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (export Bill of Entry filed with Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS) - for physical goods exports
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing export from Korea
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, or equivalent bank receipt, confirming collection of foreign currency export proceeds

Digital-service substantiation bundle for the slots and social-casino supply: Apple IAP and Google Play Billing disbursement reports, storefront country data, non-resident user sale records, and service agreements evidencing offshore performance and consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the NTS establishes that export documentation is absent, forged or untimely, or that the foreign-sourced consideration was not repatriated within 180 days or an approved extension, the supply is recharacterized as domestic taxable; the 10% VAT is assessed with statutory underpayment interest (currently 1.2% per month) and late-return penalties. Intentional or grossly negligent false zero-rating claims attract additional tax penalties and criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including penal fines up to ten times the tax understated and imprisonment, and the NTS may revoke the taxpayer's business registration and e-tax invoice entitlement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (the central bank of the Republic of Korea) as the monetary and FX infrastructure authority, operating jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the overseer of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and the Financial Supervisory Service as the bank supervisory body.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: KRW is largely convertible on the current account: royalties, service fees, wages, and profit remittances may be executed without a prior license, but each payment must be supported by an underlying contract, an invoice, a valid purpose code, and a withholding certificate where required. Capital account operations, including inbound equity contributions, share subscriptions, foreign-currency borrowings, and loans, are subject to the report-and-confirm regime of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; they are not prohibited, but they must be channelled through a licensed foreign exchange bank. There is no general forced conversion of foreign currency to KRW; companies may maintain foreign-currency deposit accounts. In practice, non-resident shareholders can remit dividends after audited financial statements are approved, corporate tax is filed, and 20-22% withholding or treaty relief is demonstrated. The principal hurdle is documentary, not exchange-control: banks require the foreign investment registration, board minutes, tax clearance, and a reconciliation of app-store revenue before releasing large outward remittances. Macro-prudential limits mainly bind banks' FX derivative positions, not ordinary commercial repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The statutory rule is a 100% repatriation and settlement requirement: all export-related foreign-currency proceeds from the digital gaming service must be received through a Korean foreign exchange bank and settled within six months of the relevant transaction date or export declaration date, unless the bank agrees to an extension for justifiable trade reasons. The mandatory KRW conversion ratio is 0% because the export proceeds may be retained in a foreign-currency account. However, the entire receipt must enter the Korean banking system and be recorded in the Foreign Exchange Information System. For App Store and Google Play receipts, the Korean publisher must keep the app store settlement statements, Apple/Google payout advices, and bank MT103 confirmation to evidence the export of services and to satisfy the bank's annual KYC review.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary banking rail. Offshore digital EMI accounts do not constitute licensed foreign exchange banks in South Korea and cannot lawfully open a settlement account or execute foreign exchange transactions for a Korean-domiciled Chusik Hoesa. Korean fintech firms holding an electronic financial business license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act may offer payment gateways and e-money settlement, but they may not accept foreign-investment capital, issue the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate, or provide foreign exchange banking services under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Corporate treasury must therefore be anchored in one of the licensed domestic tier-1 banks, with fintech payment processors used only as a supplementary collection layer for in-app store settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch physical presence is de facto mandatory for new corporate account opening at tier-1 Korean banks. At least one statutory director of the Korean entity, or a locally resident management officer delegated by board resolution, must appear in person with the corporate seal imprint, original government-issued ID, certificate of company seal registration, certificate of incorporation, and evidence of the foreign investment report. Non-resident directors are generally required to submit a formal board resolution and a notarized power of attorney apostilled at a Korean consulate; the bank will still conduct a video or face-to-face interview with each ultimate beneficial owner. Remote-only onboarding is not accepted for a medium-risk, foreign-owned simulated gaming entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders and cross-border holding structure with nominal Korean management and possible undisclosed beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified and apostilled corporate registry extract, certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, current shareholder ledger with full legal ownership genealogy, an ultimate beneficial ownership statement signed by each UBO, passport copies, proof of address less than three months old, 12-month source-of-funds bank statements, a reference letter from each UBO's regulated home-country bank, and a board resolution specifically authorising the Korean treasury relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Simulated social casino and virtual slots business could be misclassified as illegal unlicensed gambling, creating regulatory concern for the bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A legal opinion from a Korean gaming law firm confirming that the product does not satisfy the criminal definition of gambling under the Act on Game Industry Promotion and the Criminal Act because there is no real-money withdrawal, no conversion of virtual chips to legal tender, no secondary trading, and no random pay-out of cash value; the complete user terms and conditions; a compliance matrix showing age gating, responsible-gambling controls, self-exclusion limits, geo-restriction to jurisdictions that do not prohibit the game, and a no-cashout attestation; and the Game Rating and Administration Committee classification or exemption letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume micro-payment inflows from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing create a receivables pattern inconsistent with a small headcount, producing money-laundering typology signals of store-level fraud or virtual-item laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program and Google Play Developer distribution agreements; monthly store reconciliation reports from App Store Connect and Google Play Console; audited general ledger tie-out between store net revenue and bank credits; internal transaction-monitoring rules covering reversal rates, refund abuse, anomalous VIP velocity, geo-locations, and bot detection; chargeback and refund standard operating procedures with a six-month exception history; and a documented anti-money-laundering risk assessment for the social casino product from an external compliance adviser.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign payment settlement route is layered because Apple or Google may remit from Irish, Singaporean, or Hong Kong affiliates, making the direct beneficiary unclear and raising transfer-pricing and hidden-payment red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The direct contractual chain from the Korean entity to Apple Distribution International, Google Payment Corp, or other regional payment operators, showing the Korean entity as the beneficiary developer; a complete set of bank SWIFT MT103 and MT202 messages reconciled to each store payout; tax identification numbers and FATCA/CRS forms in the app store accounts; the net remittance and fee schedule; a monthly treasury ledger identifying aged offshore receivables over 90 days; and intercompany transfer-pricing documentation proving arm's-length revenue recognition and no undisclosed foreign processing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For every inbound equity injection from foreign shareholders, the investor must first submit a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The remittance should be executed as a SWIFT MT103 from the investor's overseas bank to a temporary foreign-investment capital deposit account at the Korean foreign exchange bank, with SWIFT field 70 containing the Korean company name, the investor's registered foreign-investment reference, and the phrase 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION / FIPA'. The receiving bank will issue a foreign-exchange receipt certificate, and after the share subscription and paid-in capital verification, the bank or Invest KOREA will issue the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate. The Korean company's capital verification report must be signed by a Korean certified public accountant. Funds should be converted to KRW only after bank-level FX purpose-code assignment for direct equity investment. Do not route investments through the operating current account before the FIPA report is acknowledged.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements for software royalties, game-publishing revenue share, online marketing, cloud hosting, external development, and trademark licensing should use SWIFT MT103 direct transfers with the underlying contract, a commercial invoice, proof of service delivery, and applicable tax withholding or treaty-relief certificate. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are not the efficient rail for digital services; they are appropriate only for physical goods or where a service licence beneficiary insists on bank assurance, in which case a standby letter of credit issued by the Korean bank can support the underlying payment obligations. All outward remittances must be reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System and matched against the Korean entity's service-related transaction code to avoid the bank's enhanced-review queue.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward contracts in USD/KRW and EUR/KRW for forecasted export and royalty receivables, provided the position is supported by executed underlying contracts or a low-variance annual revenue budget.
Cross-currency swaps strictly matched to foreign-currency borrowings or equity-like capital commitments, with a prior report to the Ministry of Economy and Finance where the tenor exceeds one year.
FX swaps for short-term conversion timing of app-store collections and local operating expenses, requiring the same underlying cash-flow documentation as forward transactions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted to Korean corporates for speculative purposes; they are only permissible via licensed banks as a risk-management overlay for approved non-resident investors or for the bank's own offshore book, within macro-prudential position ceilings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general shareholders' meeting and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance body; no government filing is made for the meeting itself; minutes are recorded in the corporate minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, on or before 31 March; judicial extension is available only with court approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual general meeting does not initially trigger a government fine but prevents timely approval of audited financial statements, may warrant court-ordered dissolution at the request of shareholders or creditors for persistent violation, and blocks completion of the external audit report filing with the Financial Supervisory Service before the statutory cut-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and tax reconciliation filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the third month following the end of the business year; for a calendar-year entity, 31 March; an NTS-approved filing extension is available for foreign corporations but the extension covers filing only, not tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A non-filing additional tax of 20% of the under-reported corporate tax liability is imposed, a 10% under-reporting penalty applies for omissions, 40% applies for fraudulent or evasive non-filing, and overdue delinquent tax interest accrues at approximately 0.022% per day until full payment; continued non-compliance can lead to estimated assessment, asset seizure, business closure, and cancellation of the business registration certificate by the NTS director.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax annual return and payment as a 10% surtax on corporate income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Si/Gun/Gu local government, Local Tax Division, for the registered head office or place of business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the month immediately following the NTS corporate income tax filing period; for a calendar-year entity, 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquent local corporate income tax is collected by the local authority with an unpaid local tax penalty of 3% if paid after the deadline and daily late payment interest at approximately 0.022% per day; non-payment can result in forced collection against bank accounts or receivables and administrative closure of the registered business location.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report and audited financial statements submission for companies subject to mandatory audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) DART electronic disclosure system; audited financial statements are also tabled at the annual general shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the annual general shareholders' meeting and no later than the statutory annual general meeting deadline; for a calendar-year entity, by 15 April if the annual general meeting is held on 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure by a statutorily audited company to file the audit report with the FSS may expose the company to administrative fines of up to KRW 30 million, approximately USD 22,000, and the audit opinion may be treated as not filed until remediation; this also constitutes grounds for the court to appoint an auditor and to suspend or restrict capital increases and dividend distributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate registry change registrations for officers, shareholders, registered capital, and head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent District Court, Commercial Registration Department, in the jurisdiction of the head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 calendar days from the occurrence of a registrable corporate event such as director resignation or appointment, share transfer affecting ownership, or head office relocation; a recurring annual confirmation is not required for a private Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register a change exposes the company to an administrative fine under the Commercial Act of up to KRW 5 million, approximately USD 3,700; unregistered events may not be invoked against third parties due to lack of perfection, and persistent non-registration may support dissolution proceedings by interested parties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Chusik Hoesa is legally required to obtain an independent certified CPA audit if it is listed on a Korean stock exchange or if its total assets as at the preceding fiscal year-end are at least KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 8.9 million at common reference exchange rates; additional mandatory audit triggers apply when the company is a financial-industry licensee, is a securities-listed issuer, or is otherwise designated by the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; for this ISIC 5820 software-publishing entity, turnover and headcount alone do not trigger audit, but once the quantitative asset threshold is met, the audit is compulsory and not optional.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS, Korean International Financial Reporting Standards, applies to listed and designated public companies; non-listed companies may apply K-GAAP, Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, as issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board, while K-IFRS may also be voluntarily adopted; audited financial statements must be prepared in Korean won and presented in the Korean language.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not impose a separate annual UBO return for every private Chusik Hoesa; instead, the company must maintain an accurate and up-to-date register of shareholders and must record every share transfer or issuance in that register. Changes in shareholding, including indirect ultimate beneficial ownership linked to non-resident shareholders, should be reflected in corporate and tax records and, where relevant, reported to the competent foreign exchange bank or to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act within 30 days of the transfer. For AML compliance with banks and payment providers, including Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the company must corroborate beneficial owners on a 12-month refresh cycle and notify its service providers of any material UBO change within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Officer appointments
Register of Statutory Auditors and Audit Committee members where applicable
Register of Pledged Shares and created charges or mortgages where maintained
Minute Book of shareholders' general meetings and board of directors' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 2,500 per year for a registered office address and local corporate agent or secretarial representation package in Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 18,000 per year for a small or medium private Chusik Hoesa in the software publishing sector; higher if consolidated K-IFRS reporting or a group audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top national Corporate Tax before local income tax surcharge; 26.4% combined top marginal rate after adding 10% local income tax surcharge. Progressive bands: 9% below KRW 200,000,000; 19% from KRW 200,000,000 to KRW 20,000,000,000; 21% from KRW 20,000,000,000 to KRW 300,000,000,000; 24% above KRW 300,000,000,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays are generally not available outside foreign-investment free zones; certain high-tech foreign-invested enterprises may obtain local tax reductions under the Tax Incentive Limitation Law; software and game publishing can claim R&D tax credits up to 30%-50% of qualified R&D expenses; no patent box regime; small venture companies may qualify for SME tax preferences.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return and Tax Base Statement filed via the HomeTax electronic system (www.hometax.go.kr) with attached financial statements, tax reconciliation schedules, non-resident withholding statements, and transfer pricing disclosure forms.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporations with prior-year tax payable also file semi-annual interim prepayment returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end. For a December 31 fiscal year-end, the return is due no later than March 31 of the following year; an extension of up to one month may be applied for where books or supporting documents are located abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification and shareholder information: legal name, domestic business registration number, industry code (ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210), fiscal year-end, paid-in capital, non-resident shareholder percentages, and beneficial owner list.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-controlled Chusik Hoesa must disclose the ultimate foreign parent and confirm whether it has a Korean permanent establishment. Omitting foreign control or filing as a purely local company can trigger permanent establishment attribution and DTA relief denial.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book income per Korean GAAP/IFRS financial statements: gross revenue, in-app purchase platform commissions from Apple and Google, virtual chip sales, advertising revenues, cost of sales, SG&A, operating profit, and non-operating income/expense.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue from Korean users through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing must be recognized on a gross or net basis according to the written agency and channel contracts. Non-resident equity holders should not net foreign platform fees without satisfying transfer pricing support for those commissions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income reconciliation: add-backs between book income and taxable income, including non-deductible expenses, entertainment excess, fines, donations, depreciation differences, and special reserves, and deductions such as exempt income and untaxed reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branch expenses are deductible only to the extent attributable to Korean-source income and substantiated by invoices and contracts. Interest paid to foreign related parties above the arm’s length amount is added back under thin-capitalization rules, with a 3:1 debt-to-equity safe harbor for non-financial companies and 6:1 for financial institutions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward and tax base calculation: application of prior-year net operating loss deductions, tax-exhausted income, and minimum income tax assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net operating losses for a Korean Chusik Hoesa carry forward for 10 years and cannot be carried back. A major ownership shift involving a non-resident shareholder may limit NOL utilization under continuity-of-ownership principles; a sudden restructuring before filing can invalidate carried-forward losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax calculation: apply progressive brackets to compute national CIT, then calculate the 10% local income tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches without a separate Korean entity are taxed at the same progressive rates and are also subject to branch profits tax on attributable distributable profits at 20% plus 2% local surcharge, subject to treaty reduction. The branch profits tax election and computation must be disclosed explicitly in the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and special exemptions: foreign tax credit, withholding tax credits, R&D and job creation credits, foreign-investment tax credit, and minimum tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit is available only if the Korean entity itself is the taxpayer of foreign-source income and the DTA provides for credit. A foreign parent’s taxes on its own income are not creditable against the Korean subsidiary’s CIT. A foreign tax credit claim must attach foreign tax certificates and audited computations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregation of interim prepayments, final settlement, withholding, and prior-year adjustments; computation of final tax payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident institution cannot rely solely on an overseas tax agent’s digital signature; a local authorized tax agent must submit through HomeTax and maintain a valid power of attorney. Late payment generates daily overdue interest of 0.022%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: OECD transfer pricing files and cross-border related-party disclosures: Local File, Master File index, Country-by-Country Report notification, dividend/interest/royalty withholding tax schedules, and DTA relief application forms.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent with a Korean subsidiary must sign the transfer pricing documentation, disclose intercompany transaction amounts and royalty rates, and file the withholding schedule for any dividends, royalties, or interest remitted during the year. Treaty reductions require a complete beneficial ownership certificate attached to the return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the deadline triggers additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax under the Corporate Tax Act and the National Tax Basic Act; unfaithful or fraudulent underreporting triggers an additional tax of 10% or 40% for intentional concealment, plus 0.022% daily overdue interest. Transfer pricing documentation non-submission can result in a penalty up to KRW 50,000,000 and a 20% additional assessment on unrecognized related-party amounts. Criminal referral occurs where unpaid tax exceeds KRW 300,000,000 or the false declaration is willful, with imprisonment up to 5 years under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax on non-resident dividends plus 2% local income tax surcharge, aggregating to 22% in the absence of a treaty; many South Korean treaties reduce the rate to 10% or 15% for substantial corporate shareholders and to 5% or 0% for pension funds or public-interest entities.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the foreign shareholder must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its residence tax authority, complete the Non-Resident Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction Application in HomeTax, provide a beneficial ownership declaration stating that it is not a conduit, and, if requested, submit evidence of economic substance and actual receipt of the dividend. The application must be filed with the payer before or at remittance; a retroactive refund can be filed under National Tax Basic Act procedures only where the recipient holds a valid TRC for the dividend payment date and meets the substantive requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties and interest paid to non-residents are generally 20% plus 2% local income tax surcharge, totaling 22%. Treaties commonly cap interest at 10%, with 0% for government or designated institutions in some treaties, and royalties at 10%-15%, subject to beneficial ownership and limitation-on-benefits provisions. Intercompany game software royalties, platform fees, and financing interest must not exceed arm’s length amounts; the excess is non-deductible and may be recharacterized as a dividend with additional withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where cross-border related-party transactions equal or exceed KRW 5,000,000,000; Master File is mandatory where total revenue equals or exceeds KRW 100,000,000,000 and cross-border related-party transactions equal or exceed KRW 5,000,000,000; Country-by-Country Report is mandatory where consolidated group revenue equals or exceeds KRW 1,000,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Korean tax authority applies substance-over-form under National Tax Basic Act Article 14, beneficial ownership rules, controlled foreign company rules, and thin-capitalization rules to recharacterize shell structures. A Korean Chusik Hoesa must prove that core income-generating activities, including game servicing, contract negotiation, royalty-bearing R&D decisions, financial functions, and platform control, are actually performed in Korea. Mere paper profit allocation with negligible local payroll, no local board meeting minutes, no office, and no business records exposes the entity to recharacterization of the entire Korean profit as taxable corporate income or as attributable to the foreign parent; in social casino simulation operations, journals showing Apple/Google commissions without local user-facing support and product operations will be considered artificial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring inflated deductions for intercompany management fees, virtual chip royalties, and Apple/Google platform charges paid to a foreign related entity; failing to prepare a Local File for KRW 5,000,000,000 or more of cross-border related-party transactions; or setting a zero-risk limited distributor profile while the Korean entity actually hosts and monetizes game content.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs Article 5, the tax authority may redetermine income at arm’s length; Article 9 imposes up to KRW 50,000,000 in monetary penalties for non-submission of transfer pricing documentation; additional tax of 20% or 40% for fraud applies to the understated tax; Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act provides imprisonment up to 2 years, increased to 5 years where the evaded amount exceeds KRW 300,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who approved false transfer pricing returns may be jointly liable with the corporation where corporate assets are insufficient for unpaid taxes. The director can be added as a secondary taxpayer, placed on the public delinquent list, subjected to travel blacklisting, and convicted of tax evasion with imprisonment and fines of up to twice the evaded amount; civil restitution can extend to personal bank accounts and property transfers made to shield assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and False DTA Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, interest, or royalties to a foreign parent or holding company without withholding the required 22% non-resident tax; submitting a Tax Residency Certificate for a pass-through entity that has no employees, assets, active business, or right to receive income; or failing to attach the statutory beneficial ownership form and disguising the remittance as a deductible service fee instead of a dividend.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act provisions impose withholding obligations on the payer; failure to withhold and remit triggers collection from the payer plus additional tax of 10% and daily overdue interest. A false DTA claim is treated as fraudulent underreporting with a 40% penalty, and tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act carries imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine not exceeding two times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director as withholding officer is personally liable for withheld but unremitted taxes if the corporation cannot pay. Directors face asset seizure, housing and vehicle liens, public blacklisting, and travel bans. In egregious cases, Korean courts can pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally liable where the Chusik Hoesa is a mere alter-ego or conduit of the foreign shareholder.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Economic Substance Absence and Unlicensed Real-Money Gaming / AML
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a social casino Chusik Hoesa that uses in-app purchases as disguised gambling winnings, maintains only a paper office, conducts no real local decision-making, converts virtual coins to cash through unauthorized exchanges or black-market channels, and lacks AML/CFT compliance; the Korean entity is structured solely to shop the most favorable Korean DTA and bears no real business risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: If the platform is viewed as gambling under the Criminal Act or the Game Industry Promotion Act, the business registration can be revoked, profits confiscated, and directors subjected to imprisonment up to 5 years or fines up to KRW 50,000,000. For AML failure, the Act on Financial Transactions Reports imposes monetary penalties and director prosecution. Artificial and sham transactions may be recharacterized under National Tax Basic Act Article 14 with corporate tax assessments and penalties up to 40%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors risk personal criminal liability for illegal gambling, black-market conversion, tax fraud, and money laundering. Travel bans, asset freezes, and extradition or related-country arrests may be triggered. If the company is a sham, the tax authority and courts may disregard the Chusik Hoesa’s limited liability and hold directors personally and jointly liable for unpaid taxes, civil damages, and enforcement costs, with imprisonment terms up to 7 years in serious multi-jurisdictional money-laundering schemes.
